clue.text: Precautionary marriage - no spontaneous combustion!

blocks.note: safety used as a modifier means designed to prevent harm
a match is a marriage or a good pairing

explanation.surface: A cautious wedding in which, happily, nobody bursts into flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: the whole point of this kind of match is that it lights only when struck on the box.
explanation.definitionFit: This type of match ignites only on the special strip of its box, so it will not flare up by accident.

clue.text: Injured stripper twice ran away with good friend despite the fighting

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged
letters sent away are scattered from their places, reinforcing the call to rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
the word ran written out two times
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A hurt stripper fled twice, but a good friend stood by despite the brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'friend despite the fighting' is a boxer's practice opponent: they trade punches in training yet are on the same side.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's training opponent fights them in practice sessions while actually helping them, so is an ally who exchanges blows.

clue.text: Composer of notes about student

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the musical notes are placed around the student

blocks.note: fa and la are two notes of the sol-fa scale
L is the learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A musician who writes notes about a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: In sol-fa the scale runs do, re, mi, fa, so, la, ti. Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel de Falla was the Spanish composer of the ballet The Three-Cornered Hat and Nights in the Gardens of Spain.

clue.text: Sweet delight in steamy bath?

blocks.note: surface reading: lovely pleasure while relaxing in a hot steam room
setter's reading: one nationality word goes before delight (a sweet) and before bath (a steamy one)

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word that completes both phrases: the gel-like confection dusted with sugar, and the steam-room bathhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names both a rose-flavoured jelly confection and a hammam-style steam room, so it fits sweet and bath.

clue.text: Red spy keeping mum? On the contrary!

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece is held within the other
on the contrary flips the stated relation, so it is mum that holds the spy rather than the reverse

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A communist spy keeping quiet, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red spy' and 'keeping mum' (staying silent) suggest a Cold War scene; the final phrase turns it round so that mother surrounds the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a vivid purplish-red colour, so it is one shade within the family of reds.

clue.text: Moderate not keeping god up

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the god is put within the word not
in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
Woden is the Anglo-Saxon chief god

explanation.surface: A restrained person who will not hold a deity high.
explanation.walkthrough: N(WODEN)OT read upwards gives the answer. Woden is the Old English name of Odin, who gave us Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone down something is to make it less extreme or intense, which is what moderating it means as a verb.

clue.text: Autumnal event's hot and summery - bring in right underwear before first of February

indicators.note: bring in means take inside, so the following pieces are placed within the summery word
first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
aestival is a formal word meaning of summer
R is the abbreviation for right
a vest is a sleeveless undershirt in British usage
the initial letter of the month

explanation.surface: A puzzling autumn event that is hot and summery, with underwear brought in before February.
explanation.walkthrough: The underwear and its companions go in after the first letter of the summery word. In Britain a vest is worn under a shirt, not over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The harvest festival is a church celebration of the gathered crops held in September or October, an autumn occasion.

clue.text: Head of school and professional driver with skin complaint

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letter of school
a cabby is a taxi driver, paid to drive

explanation.surface: A headteacher and a chauffeur who both suffer from a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabby skin is covered in crusts over healing sores, so the adjective describes someone with that dermatological complaint.

clue.text: German taking cover from aircraft

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the abbreviation for German swallows the covering

blocks.note: Ger is a standard abbreviation for German
a lid is a cover for a pot or box

explanation.surface: A German soldier ducking for cover from enemy planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aeroplane that flies on air currents, so it is one kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Sycophant who's hardly a streak of lightning

blocks.note: first meaning: a toady who grovels to superiors
second meaning: something that only creeps along slowly

explanation.surface: A flatterer who is hardly quick off the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A creep who fawns on the boss is called this informally, and the same word names anything that moves very slowly, like a slow lorry.

clue.text: Top brass is not particular

blocks.note: first meaning: a high-ranking army officer
second meaning: broad, applying overall rather than specifically

explanation.surface: Senior officers are not fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top brass' is collective for senior officers, but here it stands for one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a senior military rank among the top brass, and the adjective means broad or overall as opposed to specific.

clue.text: Uncivilised and hurtful remark by heretic

blocks.note: a barb is a cutting remark
an Arian followed Arius, whose teaching on Christ was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A rude, wounding comment from someone who rejects church doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarian as an adjective describes people or behaviour that is crude and lacking culture, the same as uncivilised.

clue.text: Fear of locks, perhaps

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is one such lock

blocks.note: first meaning: great anxiety or terror
second meaning: a matted rope of hair, short for a dreadlock

explanation.surface: Being afraid of locks, perhaps of being shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fear of locks' reads as a phobia; the second sense is hair, locks being tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means terror, and is also a short informal name for one matted rope of hair in a Rastafarian style.

clue.text: Over there one sees privates

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is singular

blocks.note: yon is an old word meaning that one over there
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier over there watches the private soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' looks like ranks in the army; here it means the genitals. The yoni is a Sanskrit term for the female genitals, revered in Hindu worship.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu tradition the term names the vulva, a symbol of the goddess, so it is one's private parts.

clue.text: Cropper takes Tyler for a seabird

indicators.note: takes means draws inside, so the cropper swallows the rebel's first name

blocks.note: a shearer crops the fleece from sheep
Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A farmer who crops hair hires a man named Tyler to look after a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cropper' tempts one toward a fall or a grower of crops, but here it is someone who clips sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged ocean birds that skim low over the waves, so the answer is a kind of seabird.

clue.text: Point to untrained traitors mounting futuristic defence

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, and in a down entry the letters climb from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is south, a compass point
a raw recruit is untrained
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Pointing amateur turncoats toward a sci-fi shield.
explanation.walkthrough: The name was the nickname for Reagan's 1980s Strategic Defense Initiative, a planned missile shield in space.
explanation.definitionFit: The film-derived nickname was given to the proposed American space-based missile shield of the 1980s, a defence system of the future.

clue.text: Go on at length about king being a foreigner

indicators.note: about means around, so the long-winded phrase surrounds the king

blocks.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at great length
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone rambles on about a king who is foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is a person living outside their native country, so to locals they are an outsider from abroad.

clue.text: Newly emancipated, give up a diet and settle down

indicators.note: to give up something is to abandon it, so those letters are dropped
newly means made afresh, so the remaining letters are formed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Freshly freed, someone abandons their diet and settles into life.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A, D, I, E, T from EMANCIPATED leaves E, M, A, N, C, P to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp and stay in one place, which is to settle down for a while.

clue.text: Country fellow raised in poetic subcontinent

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, and in a down entry that turns the letters bottom to top
in means placed inside, so the fellow goes within the poetic name

blocks.note: Alec is a man's name, standing for any fellow
Ind is a poetic name for India

explanation.surface: A rustic man brought up in an Indian setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country fellow' reads as a yokel, but 'Country' is the definition and 'fellow' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is an island nation in the North Atlantic, so it is an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: No tears shed for betrayal

indicators.note: shed suggests letters thrown off and scattered, so they fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody cried over a treacherous act.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Ray's biblical eye trouble

blocks.note: first meaning: a shaft of light
second meaning: the plank in your own eye in the Sermon on the Mount

explanation.surface: A man named Ray has a problem with his eyes, as in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 7 warns against noticing the mote in a brother's eye while ignoring the great timber in your own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a shaft of light and also a large timber, the one Jesus says sits in a hypocrite's own eye.

clue.text: Pests with time to pester

blocks.note: moles are garden pests that dig up lawns
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Garden pests are always around to annoy people.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest in its older sense is to bother or harass someone persistently, which is what pestering them means.

clue.text: Nurse's profession drops a point

indicators.note: drops means lets fall away, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: a career is one's profession
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A nurse's job loses some of its standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after a sick, elderly or disabled person, which is to nurse them in a broad sense.

clue.text: Basic redesign of M10 secured by airline

indicators.note: a redesign reworks the existing shape, so these letters are rearranged
secured by means held fast inside, so the reworked letters sit within the airline

blocks.note: El Al is the Israeli national airline
the letter M spelt out as its name, em, followed by 10 written as a word

explanation.surface: A fundamental overhaul of a motorway, carried out by an airline.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads M10 as a road; instead say it aloud as the letter name em and the number ten, then rearrange those letters inside the airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or rudimentary, relating to first principles, so it is a synonym of basic.

clue.text: Resin occurring in diesel emissions

indicators.note: occurring in says the word is found inside the following text

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sticky residue found in diesel exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum obtained from tropical trees and used in varnishes, ointments and perfumes.

clue.text: Not quite the end of the road in the Song of the Mystic Symbol

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is left off

blocks.clueFragment: the end of the road in the Song
blocks.note: the Burmese city at the end of the road in Kipling's ballad On the Road to Mandalay

explanation.surface: Nearly at the journey's end in the Song of the Mystic Symbol, as if a hymn title.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem, a popular song, ends each verse 'on the road to Mandalay'; Mandalay is a city in Burma (Myanmar).
explanation.definitionFit: A mandala is a circular figure representing the universe, used in Hindu and Buddhist meditation as a sacred emblem.

clue.text: On board, appear sick of harvested corn

indicators.note: being on a ship means being aboard, inside it

blocks.note: SS is a steamship, the vessel you go on board
to heave is to retch, looking about to vomit

explanation.surface: Someone on a ship looks green at the sight of the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaves are bundles of cut cereal stalks bound after reaping, so they are gathered-in grain.

clue.text: Lived in Spain with team of conservationists coming into Arab money

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so the earlier pieces go inside the currency

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a side is a sports team
NT is the National Trust, which looks after British heritage sites
the rial is the currency of several Arab states

explanation.surface: Someone lived in Spain with a team of conservationists funded by Arab cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lived in' looks like a verb phrase, but it is an adjective, as in a lived-in house. The National Trust is the British charity that owns stately homes and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential area is one where people make their homes, so it is occupied by inhabitants rather than businesses.
